svg.title: BUSINESS DISCOVERY (YELP): sketchnote
svg.text: The trap is over-engineering: the whole dataset fits on one
Ten million businesses at ~1 KB each is about 10
GB, small enough for one Postgres instance.
Keep the average rating correct under concurrent
reviews by updating it atomically in the same
Search businesses by location + radius, category, text
Leave one review per user per business; see average
Naive: WHERE lat BETWEEN … AND lng BETWEEN …. Two 1-D
B-tree indexes can't do a 2-D range efficiently.
Add a geospatial index (PostGIS GiST, ST_DWithin)
and pg_trgm for name search. 10GB fits one Postgres,
so no extra search cluster yet.
~20k searches/sec: serve reads from replicas and cache
hot business pages in Redis. The primary only takes
Reviews: a unique (user, business) constraint, and the
average updated in the same transaction as the insert,
Geohash: prefix = area, B-tree friendly; query the cell plus 8 neighbours to handle
Store sum and count; UPDATE … SET sum=sum+:r, count=count+1 in the review's
transaction. That is an atomic operation, so no lost update.
A DB unique constraint, not an application check (check-then-insert races).
Only if search needs relevance ranking, fuzzy matching, and facets beyond pg_trgm, or
A geo-sharded cluster for 10GB of data. One
Postgres with PostGIS plus replicas is enough.
Adding parts before a number shows they are
index (PostGIS, geohash), not two B-tree indexes."
